key_insight: Glioblastoma necrosis is described as an active, mutation-linked process in which tumor-recruited neutrophils form extracellular traps and amplify HMGB2-mediated tumor necroptosis.
clinical_relevance: Necrotic volume and HMGB2 expression may support prognostic stratification, while the inflammatory cascade offers potential therapeutic targets requiring further validation.
method: Integrated clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets.
Mapped tumor niches using single-cell spatial transcriptomics and protein immunofluorescence.
Investigated neutrophil-driven necroptosis in a TP53/PTEN/NF1 co-mutant mouse model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports public genomic datasets totaling n=3,639, multi-cohort clinical validation of an HMGB2-high risk signature, and preclinical disruption of the cascade with targeted anti-inflammatory compounds.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish clinical treatment benefit or provide compound identities, effect sizes, or sufficient validation details to judge therapeutic readiness.
paper_title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
